But how did the relationship between the two drivers, who have never been teammates nor fought head-to-head for a title, sour to this level?

'Princess George' and 'borderline violence'
The first sign of public animosity between the two drivers emerged following the sprint race at the 2023 Azerbaijan Grand Prix. Russell and Verstappen collided while fighting for position in the opening corners of the race, with the contact punching a hole in the side of Verstappen's Red Bull.

Staring at the damage in disbelief after the race, Verstappen, who went on to finish ahead of Russell, confronted the Mercedes driver as he walked past him in parc fermé. When Russell brushed aside Verstappen's complaints, saying "I didn't have any grip," the 29-year-old Dutchman appeared genuinely insulted and retorted, "We all had no grip!" Russell then dismissively walked away from the argument, with Verstappen calling after him, "Expect next time the same, d---head!"

The drama was caught on one of F1's roving cameras in the pit lane, making the exchange the main talking point after the race. Speaking to Dutch journalists in the paddock, Verstappen labeled his rival "Princess George," while the Mercedes driver told TV crews he was genuinely "surprised" by how angry Verstappen had been.

If nothing had followed the Baku collision, the incident could have been written off as a one-off quarrel in the heat of the moment. But over the following years, it became clear there was a serious grudge from both sides.

The next time the spat went public was at the 2024 Qatar Grand Prix, where Verstappen was given a one-place grid penalty for driving slowly on a preparation lap in qualifying. The penalty moved Russell onto pole position, but Verstappen felt his rival -- who had to take evasive action around Verstappen while on a warmup lap of his own -- had gone out of his way to get Verstappen penalized in the stewards' room.

"I find it ridiculous how [he] wants to make sure I get a penalty," Verstappen said at the time. "You know what it is? He acts decent in front of the camera here, but when you talk to him personally, he is a different person ... I can't stand that. In that case, you can better f--- off."

A week later at the final round of the season in Abu Dhabi, Russell responded to Verstappen's comments, claiming the Dutchman threatened him with "borderline violence" after the stewards' briefing.

"I find his comments pretty ironic when he comes out and says, 'I'm going to purposefully crash into you, I'm going to put you on your f---ing head in the wall.' For me, that isn't acceptable and he's gone beyond the line here, and I'm not going to accept it," Russell said. "So somebody's got to stand up to a guy like this before it gets out of control.

"All of this is racing, but he's felt the need to take it personal. I have no idea why he's done that, and he cannot deal with adversity.

"Whenever anything is not going his way, he lashes out with unnecessary anger and borderline violence. We've seen it in Brazil in the past with [Esteban] Ocon, we saw it in '21 with Lewis [Hamilton], in Mexico with Lando [Norris], in Budapest when he didn't have the most dominant car, crashes into Lewis, slamming his whole team. That is not a guy who I respect, and I wish he would be a better role model."

When Russell's quotes were put to Verstappen, it only upped the ante in the paddock's latest war of words.

"I didn't say it like that," Verstappen responded. "But you know, that's another thing. That happened behind closed doors, so you don't have to share everything that was said there and make it more dramatic.

"But you know, those things don't surprise me. I just give my opinion about how he is. Of course, he's not happy with it, but it's the same thing he did at the stewards. Lying and putting things together that aren't correct.

"He's a backstabber. It doesn't matter to me. You don't have to talk too much about people like that, they are just losers."

That same weekend in Abu Dhabi, the full F1 grid met for a dinner as part of an ongoing tradition among drivers to spend at least one evening per year as a complete group. Speaking on the "Pitstop" podcast later the same month, Liam Lawson told a story of how the weekend's bickering in the paddock spilled over to the dinner table.

"This is f---ing funny. It's really funny," Lawson said. "We rock up, at this big table. As the table was filling up, that side of the table was pretty much full, and opposite me was Max and then three chairs to the left [of him]. George hadn't turned up at this point.

"We all said, 'We're going to save the spot for George right next to Max.' George arrives and Max said, 'Mate, we've saved a seat for you.' And George just picks up the chair and walks to the other end of the table and sits with Lewis at that end of the table."

The next flashpoint came at the 2025 Spanish Grand Prix, when Verstappen crashed into the side of Russell's car -- seemingly out of pure frustration. The collision happened shortly after a late safety car period had left Verstappen on worn tires in the fight against his rivals and scuppered his chances of a podium finish.

Russell attempted a move on Verstappen at Turn 1 that resulted in the Mercedes driver sliding into Verstappen, forcing the Red Bull driver off the track. The stewards launched an investigation into the incident, which Red Bull feared might result in Verstappen receiving a penalty for leaving the track and gaining an advantage.

Verstappen's engineer, Gianpiero Lambiase, radioed his driver to tell him to give the position back to Russell to avoid a potential penalty -- much to the frustration of Verstappen. On the approach to Turn 5 on the following lap, Verstappen appeared to cede the position to Russell, only to accelerate again before the apex and collide with the Mercedes.

The stewards deemed Verstappen entirely at fault for the collision and issued a 10-second penalty -- dropping him to 10th place at the finish -- as well as three penalty points on his superlicense, bringing him just a single point from a race ban. Although Verstappen later admitted the incident "should not have happened" in an Instagram post -- as close to an apology as you'll likely get from the Red Bull driver -- Russell still took the opportunity to take a sideways dig at his rival.

"I was a bit surprised to see him taking responsibility, because it's quite unlike him," he said. "We actually bumped into each other at the airport a few days ago, but we didn't even chat about it. He was there with his family and his newborn, chatting about how that was going. He was busy folding the pram and trying to get it through the security scanner.

"Had I been taken out of the race, I'd be feeling very differently for sure. Ultimately, his actions benefitted me, cost him, and I should say thanks."

The pair then lined up on the front row of the grid for the next race in Canada, leading Russell to make a pointed joke about how close Verstappen was to a race ban.

"We're mates so it's all good," Russell said when asked about the potential for a collision at the first corner. "I've got a few more points on my license to play with! So ... let's see."

Verstappen was said to be annoyed by the comments and another row broke out after the race when Red Bull tried to get Russell disqualified for driving erratically behind a safety car. Verstappen had briefly overtaken Russell when the Mercedes driver hit the brakes to warm his tires behind the safety car, and Red Bull protested the move following the race, only for the appeal to be thrown out by the stewards several hours later.

As an aside, but another example of Verstappen's tendency to hold a grudge, the incident with Russell at the Spanish Grand Prix was referenced in the postrace news conference at the season-deciding Abu Dhabi Grand Prix. When a journalist asked Verstappen if he regretted the incident given that he lost the title by fewer points than the penalty cost him in Spain, the Red Bull driver responded, "You forget all the other stuff that happened in my season. The only thing you mention is Barcelona. I knew that would come. You're giving me a stupid grin now."

Nearly four months later, at this year's Japanese Grand Prix, Verstappen refused to start his news conference until the same journalist had left the room.

What happened in Vegas is unlikely to stay in Vegas
Coming back up to speed under the bright lights of Las Vegas on Saturday night, and Russell and Verstappen spent the first half of the race trading position at the front of the field -- invariably with Verstappen coming out on top.

Russell, who desperately needed a victory to salvage something from the most bruising season of his career, appeared to be overdriving each time he got his nose ahead of the Red Bull. If Russell took the lead into Turn 14, Verstappen always had an answer, whether it came through the high-speed Turn 17 on the following straight or by waiting for Russell to go deep at Turn 1 and retaking the position in Turns 2, 3 and 4.

Things got worse for Russell on lap 38 when he slipped behind teammate Kimi Antonelli to third place, meaning as the laps counted down, he needed to do something extra special to move up two positions and salvage victory.

With two laps of the 50-lap race remaining, he resorted to a high-risk, late-braking attempt on Antonelli at Turn 5. Only a few drivers had made such a pass stick all evening, and as Russell found himself off the racing line, a combination of debris and dust resulted in a lock-up and light contact with the barrier in the run-off area.

"Ha ha, well done! My God," Verstappen laughed over team radio as he watched events unfold behind him.

Russell managed to extricate his car from the barrier, but the time lost returning to the track meant he could only manage a ninth-place finish at the checkered flag.

Verstappen's desire to comment so publicly about Russell's misfortune was notable and no doubt at the front of his mind due to an incident between the two drivers during final practice in Las Vegas the day before.

A loose gentleman's agreement exists between drivers to wait in line to start a fast lap in practice, and Verstappen essentially tried jumping the queue ahead of Russell on the back straight toward the end of the session. Russell, aggrieved by the move, then attempted to repass Verstappen ahead of Turn 14 -- the last braking zone before the start of a new lap -- but in doing so was squeezed to the inside of the track by the Red Bull, resulting in a light brush of wheels between the two cars at the apex.

In the eyes of the stewards, the incident only warranted giving a warning to Verstappen for movement under braking, but in the furious microclimate of the Verstappen-Russell rivalry, it added fuel to the fire once more.

Speaking after the qualifying session that followed final practice, Russell built on his previous rhetoric that Verstappen acts like a paddock bully.

"I am not just going to accept somebody to screw me over like this and walk around like they are bigger and better than everyone else," Russell said. "Somebody has got to stand up to that guy."

Immediately after qualifying, Verstappen refused to acknowledge the practice incident but couldn't resist sticking the knife in after his victory on Saturday. In an interview with Dutch broadcaster Viaplay, he was asked if the win had been in some way been inspired by Russell's quotes the previous day.

"His comments don't motivate me, because he's nowhere near me," Verstappen responded. "All talk off the track and a complete joke on it this season. Perfect karma."

The 2026 title battle may be over, but the drama in the F1 paddock never stops. Expect this one to continue at the final two rounds in Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

stories.headline: Fantasy basketball adds and NBA bets: Expect Bulls, Nuggets to score
stories.summary: Jim McCormick breaks down Sunday's NBA slate, highlighting the fantasy streamers to add and bets to make.
stories.body:
Today's seven-game schedule is defined by a series of competitive matchups. Sunday's biggest spread is just 9.5 points. Tighter point spreads suggest more predictable playing patterns, with key players positioned to sustain their usual workloads deep into the fourth quarter. We covet these games for the blend of floor and ceiling they offer both our redraft and daily fantasy choices, with that same clarity helping to inform our approach to totals and player props.

According to today's lengthy injury report, the Oklahoma City Thunder will be without seven rotation players against the Miami Heat. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is listed as questionable due to lower back soreness after enduring a hard fall in the team's recent win over the New Orleans Pelicans.

On the other side of the floor, Giannis Antetokounmpo is questionable as a result of a groin issue. Given Oklahoma City's atypical depth, players like Ajay Mitchell, Jared McCain and the twin-tower centers could still make things competitive in both real and fantasy contexts.

The day of hoops opens with the Detroit Pistons visiting the Atlanta Hawks for a matinee matchup. The Hawks won't have CJ McCollum for the next month due to a calf strain, while Detroit is without both Jalen Duren and Duncan Robinson. The questions for Detroit remain secondary scoring and playmaking, although a certain Motown combo guard among the streaming options below could provide the answer.

After resting last night, we can expect Jayson Tatum back for the Boston Celtics against the Golden State Warriors this evening.

The most inviting offensive climate today is found in Illinois, with the suddenly surging Chicago Bulls hosting the Denver Nuggets in a game that sports the highest projected point total of the day by a wide margin. Finding paths into both rotations could be rewarding, making this matchup a focus of today's streaming options.

Fantasy stream team
Players available in at least 50% of leagues

Christian Braun, SG/SF, Nuggets (rostered in 50.8% of ESPN leagues)
Approaching Dyson Daniels' tier of larceny, Braun is averaging nearly three steals per game over the past week and well over two per game for the season. The Bulls are loose with the ball and quick with possessions, setting up Braun with a nice blend of transition, catch-and-shoot, and turnover-fueled opportunities today.

Daniss Jenkins, PG, Pistons (40.4%)
Averaging 19 points, five rebounds, and just over four assists over the past week, Jenkins has emerged as a critical co-pilot for Cade Cunningham as the Pistons have remained competitive against contenders -- despite missing two huge contributors to the rotation. Jenkins should see plenty of touches and time on the ball today.

Aday Mara, C, Thunder (35.1%)
Clearly ready to handle a large role as a rookie, Mara is thriving in a twin-towers role alongside Isaiah Hartenstein. The Michigan product is a gifted interior scorer and proven rim protector. With the Thunder missing so many rotation members, Mara will touch the ball often today.

Kelly Oubre Jr., SF/SG, Pacers (12.5%)
The Pacers are already without Tyrese Haliburton, while Pascal Siakam is listed as questionable for this evening's game versus the New York Knicks. Even if Siakam is active, expect Oubre to stay busy slashing, driving, and shooting for a team that simply needs offensive creation.

Tre Jones, PG, Bulls (8.1%)
If you need dimes, this is your guy. If you need points, rebounding, or a big haul of 3-pointers, this is not your guy. Assists are difficult to source from free agency given how often teams are empowering stars from all over the floor to handle creation duties. Jones is an old-school pure point guard in that he's there to keep the Chicago offense organized, to whatever degree that's sustainable. If you need frontcourt support, look to teammate Nic Claxton.

Jaxson Hayes, C, Utah Jazz (13.8%)
The Jazz entered the season with suspect depth at center. With multiple veteran big men sidelined for Utah, Hayes has shifted in a steady, starting role. Averaging a double-double and nearly 27 minutes across his past two games, Hayes is in a strong spot today against a deep Dallas frontcourt.

Jim's bets to make on Sunday
Odds by DraftKings and subject to change.

Onyeka Okongwu OVER 14.5 points (-118)

Atlanta's stretch center has averaged 22 points and 35 minutes in the team's two games without CJ McCollum. His usage rate has risen by 4.07 percentage points with McCollum off the floor this season -- the largest increase of any Hawks player. That blend of sustained playing time and added scoring opportunities makes this an achievable number.

Matas Buzelis over 1.5 assists (-127)

Chicago's matchup with Denver carries the slate's highest projected total, offering a favorable setting for Buzelis to collect a couple of assists. He's been getting consistent minutes and has cleared this mark in all but three of his last 10 games. His passing production can fluctuate, but the modest target and scoring expectations make this a reasonable play.

Jamal Murray over 23.5 points (-111)

Chicago allows the fourth-most PG points and struggles to defend the paint, where Murray gets a third of his scoring. The Bulls also send opponents to the foul line often and play at the league's fastest pace. That combination should give Murray plenty of scoring chances in the game with today's highest projected total.

stories.headline: Auston Matthews 'embarrassed' as Leafs blow another lead in loss to Columbus
stories.summary: Auston Matthews says the Maple Leafs "should be embarrassed" after two goals in less than a minute against the Blue Jackets doomed Toronto to another loss.
stories.body:
Toronto Maple Leafs captain Auston Matthews called his team's performance "inexcusable" following their 4-3 loss on Saturday night to the visiting Columbus Blue Jackets, extending their winless streak to nine games.

"It's obviously been a really rough stretch here, but tonight, we should be embarrassed," Matthews told reporters. "It's not fair to the people who pay for tickets to come and watch. It's inexcusable."

The Maple Leafs are 0-8-1 over their past nine, including Thursday's blown 3-0 lead against the Los Angeles Kings that ended in a 4-3 shootout loss, and have won just one of their previous 12 games (1-10-1).

Maple Leafs winger William Nylander turned the puck over in his own zone before Matthew Knies scored against his former team to tie the game 3-3 with under five minutes to go in regulation. Zach Werenski then scored the game winner 52 seconds later as the Blue Jackets won their second straight game.

"We just threw up all over ourselves pretty much and lose the game," defenseman Jake McCabe told reporters. "... It's hard to wrap your head around, that's for sure.

"I thought our fans were engaged all game and into it and loud. I'd be pissed off too if I were them."

The next chance for the Maple Leafs to avoid the winless streak stretching to 10 games comes at the New York Islanders on Monday.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Columbus coach says Messi should've got red card in Miami loss: 'Everyone knows'
stories.summary: Columbus Crew head coach Laurent Courtois said Lionel Messi should have received a red card for taking a throw-in straight into the face of Gonzalo Tapia.
stories.body:
MIAMI -- Columbus Crew head coach Laurent Courtois said Lionel Messi should have received a red card for throwing the ball into the face of Gonzalo Tapia during the Crew's 3-0 victory over Inter Miami on Saturday night at Nu Stadium.

With Tapia not backing off the required distance, Messi took a quick throw-in straight into the face of the Crew forward from just a couple of feet away.

Messi and Tapia both received yellow cards from referee Allen Chapman for the incident, which occurred in first-half stoppage time of Game 1 of the best-of-three round one playoff series.

Had Messi received a red card, he would have been suspended for at least the next game.

"Everyone knows that was more than a yellow card," Courtois told reporters after the match.

The Crew coach added that the entire situation is "sad," when asked if he thought Major League Soccer should review the incident.

Tapia, who scored twice for Columbus in the win, did not weigh in on the referee's decision.

"It's a play in the match. I don't know if it's a red card, but I am not the referee to say," he said. "It stays there."

Inter Miami head coach Cristian "Kily" González adopted a similar tone when asked about the incident.

"I have to think about the situation, the card doesn't change much," he said in his postgame news conference. "The referee saw a yellow and that is it, we can't blame the referee. Sometimes they make mistakes, sometimes they don't like each one of us and we have to accept it."

Miami, the 2026 MLS Cup winner, now faces the possibility of a first-round elimination after entering the playoffs as the second seed in the Eastern conference.

Miami must win in Columbus on Friday to earn a third match at Nu Stadium to keep its playoff hopes alive.

"Pressure? Of course there is pressure," Miami's Brazilian defender/midfielder Casemiro said. "Inter Miami always plays to win and we know if we lose the next game we are out. So, that's the pressure.

"The most important thing now is to be calm. We know we have to do better, because we can do better. We were second on the table and so the next game we'll use it to show the rest how strong we are."

Ahead of kickoff on Saturday, Inter Miami co-owner Jorge Mas presented Messi with the 2026 Golden Boot award, which the star won earlier this month.

Messi also won the Golden Boot last year, becoming the first player to win the award given to the league's top scorer in consecutive seasons.

He had 26 goals during the regular season, along with 17 assists -- second-most in the league. He's just the sixth MLS player to win multiple Golden Boots. He is also expected to win his third straight MLS MVP award.

Information from The Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.headline: DiBernardo joins Rapinoe, Pulisic in pantheon of great Olimpicos
stories.summary: Vanessa DiBernardo joined an elite list on Saturday, scoring for Kansas City direct from a corner. Known in soccer circles as an Olimpico, here are some of the very best.
stories.body:
(Editor's note: This article was originally published on Oct. 2, 2025, and it has been updated after Vanessa DiBernardo's stunner in Saturday's NWSL championship finale.)

For a relatively simple sport, soccer is filled with novelties.

Outfield players don the gloves and go into goal when there's no other option, penalty takers attempt chipped "Panenka" spot kicks to varying degrees of success, goalkeepers sprint the length of the pitch to come up for last-minute corners -- and sometimes they even score. And every now and then, players will score directly from a corner kick.

Highly improbable, sometimes intentional, a goal scored in this way is known as a Gol Olimpico, an Olympic goal.

But how did these goals get their name? The history of the Olimpico is irrevocably intertwined with South American football and with one of its great rivalries: Uruguay vs. Argentina.

- New Premier League record set with eight injury-time goals

- From World Cup Willie to Ciao: Ranking every World Cup mascot

- NWSL has more money than ever, yet its biggest problems remain

On June 9, 1924, Uruguay won the Olympic gold medal in Paris after defeating Switzerland 3-0. Around the same time in June 1924, the International Football Association Board (IFAB) changed the laws around corner kicks, making goals scored directly from the corner legal. But it wasn't until Oct. 2, 1924, that these two pieces of information would combine to create the Olimpico moniker.

Following Uruguay's Olympic victory, they played a two-game friendly series with their South American neighbors Argentina. The teams played out a 1-1 draw in Montevideo in late-September before travelling to Buenos Aires.

The return match was suspended after four minutes due to the large crowd on the sideline and was rescheduled for Oct. 2. Argentina would eventually win the rematch 2-1, but the whole game was filled with controversy. La Celeste withdrew from the match with four minutes remaining and both sides accused the other of excessive aggression.

But the important part of this story happened in the 15th minute, when Argentina's Cesareo Onzari whipped in a corner and scored.

The audacity of the goal and La Albiceleste defeating the Olympic champions was the catalyst for local journalists to dub the goal an Olympic one. From then on, whenever other goals were scored in this fashion, they were described as like the one scored against the Olympians, and soon the label Gol Olimpico was applied to all such goals.

The Olimpico is stunning when it's intentional and sometimes comical when it's not. It really has no right to work considering where players are standing on the field, how much of the target they can see from that position and what they need to do to the ball to make it curve into the back of the net. Whether they dribble through at the near post or sail past everyone into the far corner, there's beauty in the curl of ball, the audacity, the incredulity. It's glorious.

Take Vanessa DiBernardo's opening goal in Saturday's NWSL championship game. The Kansas City Current were set on course for their first NWSL title thanks to DiBernardo's Olimpico in the 54th minute, with the ball curling over everyone's head to nestle into the far corner of the next.

From regular-season matches to finals, the Olympics and even the World Cup, here are some of the very best Olimpicos.

Vanessa DiBernardo, Kansas City Current vs. Washington Spirit | 2026 NWSL championship

Kansas City fans will never forget how the Current's first NWSL championship was secured thanks in large part to DiBernado's kick from the corner. Hang it in the Louvre.

Marcos Coll, Colombia vs. USSR | 1962 World Cup

The most impressive part of the first Olimpico to be scored at a World Cup is who Coll beat in the USSR goal: the legendary Lev Yashin.

Megan Rapinoe, United States vs. Canada | 2012 London Olympics

When it comes to scoring an Olimpico at the Olympics, only one player in soccer history has managed the feat: USWNT icon Rapinoe.

Elise Kellond-Knight, Australia vs. Norway | 2019 Women's World Cup

The Matildas may have got knocked out of the 2019 Women's World Cup on penalties, but they'll always have Kellond-Knight's amazing Olimpico at the Allianz Riviera in Nice.

Leandro Carvalho, Ceará vs. Corinthians | 2019-20 Brazilian Serie A

Carvalho's Olimpico was cunning and spectacular, catching the defence sleeping and using the outside of his foot. What's more, it was scored in the 92nd minute to level the scores at 2-2 against São Paulo giants Corinthians.

Megan Rapinoe, United States vs. Australia | 2020 Tokyo Olympics

Remember when we said that Rapinoe was the only player in soccer history to score an Olimpico at the Olympic Games? Well she's did it twice, repeating her 2012 stunner over eight years later in Tokyo.

Hakan Çalhanoglu, Internazionale vs. AS Roma | 2020-21 Serie A

Why is Çalhanoglu's goal against AS Roma -- in Rome -- so memorable? It's an Olimpico at the Stadio Olimpico of course! How good.

Kyra Cooney-Cross, Melbourne Victory vs. Sydney FC | 2020-21 A-League Women

In the 120th minute of the A-League Women Grand Final, 19-year-old Cooney-Cross stepped up to take a corner ... and wrote her name into Australian football folklore.

Katie Zelem, Manchester United vs. Leicester City | 2021-22 Women's Super League

Scoring one Olimpico is hard enough, but Zelem managed to do it twice in one game. What's more, Zelem scored an Olimpico in the match before this one too.

Katie McCabe, Republic of Ireland vs. Canada | 2023 Women's World Cup

In their first appearance at a Women's World Cup, captain McCabe made sure Ireland fans would never forget the tournament with this inspirational strike.

Christian Pulisic, AC Milan vs. Club Brugge | 2024-25 UEFA Champions League

USMNT star Pulisic called it "a bit of luck" at the time, but there's no doubting the quality of his strike for AC Milan in their 3-1 win over Club Brugge in last season's Champions League league phase.

Son Heung-Min, Tottenham Hotspur vs. Manchester United | 2024-25 Carabao Cup

No Olimpico list would be complete without Son's stunner that sent Manchester United packing in the 2024-25 Carabao Cup quarterfinals. The South Korea skipper's crazy 88th-minute strike was the perfect denouement of a topsy-turvy match that finished 4-3 after Spurs had been leading 3-0.

Ángel Di María, Rosario Central vs. Boca Juniors | 2025 Liga Profesional de Fútbol

Last, but certainly not least, is this beauty from Di María for Rosario Central in their 1-1 draw with Boca Juniors in September. The Argentina star has a habit of scoring from corners, with this one -- astonishingly -- his fourth Olimpico.
